I was a Digg refugee when I came to Reddit. There was the whole V4 debacle but that was really just the catalyst to a lot of stuff that was bubbling under the surface. Among the behind the scenes annoyances were the people branded Digg Patriots who were rabidly conservative and would "digg" their opinions and bury any dissenting ones. I'm neither republican nor democrat, but personally hate when reasonable discussion is systematically drowned out. Next on the list were the comments. They just kept getting more and more immature to the point where "Fuck reLIEgion" would be at the top of the thread. Once the V4 train wreck was in full effect every thread had a post to try Reddit and Digg sucks. People were ready to find a new alternative. The when Kevin Rose was completely nonchalant about what people saying (screaming) that was the final straw.

I see a lot of different stories here and none really match my account; most are just general things like "the site design changed".

The reason why Digg fell is really two fold. One of those folds is really similar to what's going on with reddit right now and that is what's showing up on the site is being controlled by a limited number of users. In Digg's case it was the Patriots. Digg operated a little differently than reddit in that the better your submissions were Dugg (upvoated) then the better the chance you had at reaching the front page. This created a positive feedback loop which only a very limited number of users ever had content listed on the front page. Digg tried to mitigate this and every change they made really didn't work, it only made the problem worse. Another thing you have to remember is that back in those days the concept of subverses or subreddits didn't exist, it was all just one page and it was moderated by the people who ran the site. So reddit's current problem with power moderators censoring content they don't agree with really wasn't a problem either site could have. Still the effect is similar in that a limited number of power moderators control most of the content of the default subs and have a much stronger "vote" on what gets to the front page.

For me the biggest reason to finally hang up Digg is that reddit had a promise that everybody's vote was equal. You had equal influence on what was being discussed as anyone else. I believe the current state of reddit is failing to deliver that promise.

The second fold has to do with the redesign and corporate influence. This both has to do with Digg allegedly being paid to make a post look like it was properly dugg to the front page, but more with corporate shills creating accounts digging each other's links, and then when those accounts have power; just putting whatever story they wanted on the front page themselves (again Digg was constantly playing with the algorithm to prevent this from happening). Their final solution to this was not received well at all, this is what people call Digg 4.0. It was really their attempt at subreddits/subverses, but it was more like an RSS feed. So for instance if you wanted to subscribe to Burger King's account and get all their posts, you could. Or for that matter the Nintendo, Playstation, Microsoft, Apple, Kotaku, Engadget, NBC News, etc... accounts. I for one really liked the redesign as it allowed you to better regulate what reached your front page. However the subscriptions weren't billed as subscribing to something like Technology, or Advice Animals, or Ask Digg. Also if you subscribed to one account, that account was managed by just one person; not a team of community moderators.

So with the continued dissatisfaction of users not believing that their diggs counted equally, and Digg's continued failures to create a viable solution, many many users fled Digg for reddit after the v4 redesign. They had a much better solution to Digg's problems and it was really a fresh restart for everybody.

Personally right now I think we're in the first fold of reddit's decline. People are unhappy that the power of the few influences what is on the front page, and what is discussed. They are very close to aggravating the majority of their user base and causing them to flee. This continued talk of Safe Spaces is very troubling and could be signaling a redesign similar to Digg v4.0, but we'll just have to wait and see.
